title: Proper direct-image constructibility
statement:
Every proper morphism
between schemes of finite type over $k$ satisfies
$\mathcal C(f)$ of [def-finrepair-property-c].

proof.text: Fix the finite ring $\Lambda$ and allowable coefficients in [def-finrepair-property-c], and a proper $k$-morphism $f:X\to S$ with $X,S$ of finite type over the field $k$. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ and $S$ Noetherian. In particular they are quasi-compact, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes them quasi-separated. The assertion concerns each $R^qf_*F$ individually and introduces no uniform bound on $q$.

source.place: Proof, first and last paragraphs; Stacks 01T6 and 01OY

proof.text: It suffices to prove the assertion when $S$ is affine. For an affine open $a:S_0\hookrightarrow S$, let $X_0=f^{-1}(S_0)$ and $f_0:X_0\to S_0$. Properness of $f_0$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Every open in a Noetherian scheme is quasi-compact: otherwise finite unions of members of an open cover have no maximal member, and their closed complements have no minimal member, contrary to [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. All these opens are of finite type over $k$: choose finitely many affine charts in the Noetherian open, and within each original finite-type affine chart use finitely many principal opens, whose rings are localizations at one element and hence finitely generated over $k$. For a constructible $F$, restricting its finite locally closed partition shows that $F|_{X_0}$ is constructible, by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] to $F[0]$ and take cohomology: $(R^qf_*F)|_{S_0}\cong R^qf_{0,*}(F|_{X_0})$, since inverse image on constant-coefficient modules is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. If the affine-target assertion holds, each of these restrictions is constructible. Apply the open-local equivalence (2) iff (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-qcqs-affine-local] on the qcqs scheme $S$. This proves $\mathcal C(f)$ globally.

Now fix an affine target $S$. For each closed subset $Z\subseteq X$, give it its reduced induced closed subscheme structure, and put $f_Z:Z\to X\xrightarrow{f}S$. The closed-immersion and composition clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] make $f_Z$ proper. These closed subschemes are of finite type over $k$: on finite affine charts their rings are quotients of finitely generated $k$-algebras. The empty closed subset has the property, because its sheaf category is zero and all its direct images are zero; the zero sheaf is constructible by the defining finite partition condition of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. If any closed subset fails $\mathcal C(f_Z)$, choose an inclusion-minimal failing subset using [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. It is nonempty, and every proper closed subset of it satisfies the property.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: Noetherian induction (minimal-counterexample form); Stacks 01W5, 01W3 and 01OZ

proof.text: For this minimal $Z$, the hypotheses of [lem-fin-noetherian-chow-modification] hold: the target $S$ is affine Noetherian, $f_Z$ is proper, and $Z$ is reduced. Obtain a proper $\pi:Y\to Z$ and a dense open $U\subseteq Z$ with $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ an isomorphism and $f_Z\pi:Y\to S$ projective. The scheme $Y$ is of finite type over $k$: the projective definition [def-pc-projective-morphism] realizes it as a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^r_S$, whose standard affine charts are polynomial algebras over the finite-type affine $S$; the finite chart cover proves finite type. Thus [thm-fin-projective-constructibility-complete] gives $\mathcal C(f_Z\pi)$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: Chow modification and the projective case

proof.text: Let $W=Z\setminus U$ have its reduced induced structure and let $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$. Density and nonemptiness of $Z$ imply $W\subsetneq Z$, so minimality gives $\mathcal C(f_Zi)$; the reduction of $W$ as a subscheme of $Z$ is the same reduced induced subscheme of $X$. Both $f_Z$ and $\pi$ are proper finite-type maps, $\pi$ is an isomorphism over $U$, and the two required constructibility predicates have just been obtained. Apply [lem-finrepair-modification-c] to conclude $\mathcal C(f_Z)$, contradicting the choice of $Z$. Consequently every reduced closed subscheme of $X$, including $X_{\mathrm{red}}$, has constructible higher direct images to $S$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: complement induction and modification transfer

proof.text: Put $r:X_{\mathrm{red}}\hookrightarrow X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $r$ is a universal homeomorphism. The equivalence of small etale topoi in [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance] identifies inverse and direct images as quasi-inverse exact functors; the same holds for $\Lambda$-modules because the equivalence preserves products and therefore carries the scalar-action map and its associativity and unit identities to the corresponding maps and identities, with the inverse equivalence reversing this construction. For constructible $F$ on $X$, the sheaf $r^{-1}F$ is constructible: pull back its finite partition; on each stratum pull back an etale covering that trivializes the sheaf with a finite module as value, which is again a covering and gives the same finite module as value, as in [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The constant-coefficient module functor and its exactness are those of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Choose an injective resolution $I$ of $r^{-1}F$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives]: embed in an injective, take its cokernel, and repeat to obtain the bounded-below resolution.  The exact equivalence $r_*$ preserves injectives: a monomorphism and a map into $r_*J$ pull back under its exact inverse to a monomorphism and a map into $J$; injectivity extends that map, and applying $r_*$ gives the required extension. Thus $r_*I$ resolves $r_*r^{-1}F\cong F$. For each etale $V\to S$, the direct-image formula of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives $(f_*r_*I)(V)=I(X_{\mathrm{red}}\times_SV)=((fr)_*I)(V)$, with identical restriction maps and differentials. Hence $R^qf_*F\cong R^q(fr)_*r^{-1}F$. The right side is constructible by the result for $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ in step 5. This proves the affine-target assertion, and step 2 proves the item.
